# Embedded text fixtures

These are synthetic test assets generated by `scripts/generate-embedded-native-fixtures.py`, using ReportLab 4.5.1 and fontTools 4.62.1. Native tests consume checked-in assets without Python dependencies.

- `reportlab-subset.pdf` contains two colored text runs created by ReportLab with its ordinary simple TrueType subset encoding. It exercises real PDFium Unicode extraction and font reuse.
- `DejaVuSerif-subset.ttf` contains only the glyphs needed by native CID and WinAnsi fixtures, which `src-tauri/tests/embedded_text.rs` builds in temporary directories.
- `DejaVuSerif-conflicting-cmap.ttf` deliberately changes the Windows Unicode mapping for E to the O glyph while retaining the correct platform-0 mapping. Original text remains unaffected; introducing E must be refused.
- `DejaVuSerif-missing-cmap.ttf` instead removes the Windows mapping for E. A present/missing disagreement must also be refused.

All font files are derived from the existing `../corpus/fonts/DejaVuSerif.ttf`. The full copyright, permission, and redistribution notices are in `../corpus/fonts/LICENSE_DEJAVU.txt`; these notices apply to all three subset files and the font embedded in the PDF. DejaVu changes are public domain; the underlying Bitstream and Arev license terms remain applicable. The subset names contain neither reserved name Bitstream nor Vera. Generated document text and fixture-generation code are covered by this repository's MIT license. No ReportLab or fontTools implementation code or font data is copied into these assets.

`manifest.json` records generated asset sizes and SHA-256 checksums.
